title.narrative: Provision of legal protection services for vulnerable displaced population in Gaza

description.narrative: ltpgtNRC will provide legal information, counselling, and assistance (ICLA) to ensure vulnerable populations in need of legal support obtain vital civil, identity, travel, family, guardianship, and other documentation, granting them access to essential services. The project will also provide awareness-raising and legal aid on topics including collaborative dispute resolution methodologies to safeguard housing, land, and property (HLP) rights, addressing eviction threats, land disputes, and tenure security issues. ltbrgt ltbrgtThrough this proposed project, NRC, in collaboration with the Palestinian Bar Association (PBA), will aim to support a total of 19,008 individuals (9,504 F/ 9,504M) in northern Gaza, prioritizing women-/children-headed households, Internally Displaced Populations (IDPs), refugees subjected to torture and ill-treatment, and persons with disabilities (PwDs), by employing a network of field lawyers, mobile legal aid clinics, hotlines, and printed/digital media. ltbrgt ltbrgtSpecifically, 8,400 project participants will receive information on civil and legal identity documents and HLP issues (4,200 NRC/4,200 PBA). 6,365 project participants will receive counselling on civil and identity documents and HLP rights, of which 2,693 on legal identity (1,346 NRC/1,347 PBA) and 3,672 on HLP (1,836 NRC/1,836 PBA). 2,448 project participants will receive para-legal and legal assistance on HLP issues (1,224 NRC/1,224 PBA), and 1,795 (898 NRC/897 PBA) participants will receive para-legal and legal assistance on civil and legal identity documents. In total, 1,632 civil, identity, and HLP documents will be restored/obtained, 1,142 civil and identity documents (571 by each NRC and PBA), and 490 HLP documents (245 by each NRC and PBA). ltbrgt ltbrgtThe project will include a cash assistance modality to help participants cover administrative fees, photocopying costs, transportation, and court fees. This targeted financial support will decrease economic barriers, which often prevent individuals from obtaining legal documentation or resolving land disputes. By ensuring equitable access to legal services, NRC will enhance protection outcomes, empowering vulnerable populations to secure their rights and navigate complex legal processes. ltbrgt ltbrgtBy implementing these strategic approaches, NRC will empower individuals with legal tools to reclaim rights, access services, and strengthen resilience. Thus, this project will contribute to legal protection, improved humanitarian outcomes, and enhanced recovery for displaced and conflict-affected populations. ltbrgtlt/pgt
